Definition: a hollow, i.e. vessel used as a (dry) measure
BiblicalUsage: A cab is a small dry measure, and it shows up once, in the famine of besieged Samaria, when the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung sold for five pieces of silver.
TheologicalSignificance: I read that price as the measure of the famine: when a handful of filth costs silver, the city has nothing left.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
